events.title: Where I’m From
events.description: Works created by artists from Mural Arts Philadelphia’s Rec Crew and SCI Phoenix.

events.title: The Battle of the Bathers
events.description: Learn about the controversy between Dr. Barnes and the Philadelphia Museum of Art around works by Paul Cézanne.

events.title: Henri Rousseau: A Painter’s Secrets
events.description: See the inventive works of Henri Rousseau in a new light.

events.title: The Doctor and the Douanier: How Dr. Barnes Built His Collection of Rousseaus
events.description: The story behind the world’s largest collection of Rousseaus.

events.title: Revolutionary Botany
events.description: Tracing the evolution of medicine in America from medicinal plants to the modern pharmacy. Part of the Mütter Museum's 2026 programming celebrating medical milestones throughout the past 250 years.

events.title: Ancient Egypt in Watercolors: Paintings and Artifacts from Dra Abu el-Naga
events.description: Century-old watercolors by Egyptian artist Ahmed Yousef capturing New Kingdom tomb chapels from Dra Abu el-Naga, Thebes. First rotation through June; second rotation from July through November ahead of the Egypt Galleries grand reopening.

events.title: Botany of Nations
events.description: The Lewis and Clark expedition retold through an Indigenous lens. Plants act as portals to under-shared stories, cultures, and sciences of the Indigenous peoples encountered on the journey. Created in collaboration with Indigenous-led nonprofit Local Contexts.

events.title: James Santangelo's Late Night Jam
events.description: James Santangelo 'is a force to be reckoned with on piano' and is a committed musician on the Philadelphia jazz scene. A late-night jam session open to all.

events.title: Freedom Dreams
events.description: A meditation on the memories, dreams, and histories of America, featuring powerful works by contemporary moving-image artists Arthur Jafa, David Hartt, Garrett Bradley, Ja’Tovia Gary, and Tourmaline.

events.title: A Nation of Artists
events.description: The most expansive presentation of American art ever mounted in Philadelphia. Featuring more than 1,000 works across PMA and PAFA, celebrating the museum's 150th anniversary and the nation's 250th.

events.title: Legionnaires' Disease: The Philadelphia Outbreak
events.description: Examining Philadelphia's headline-grabbing 1976 outbreak of Legionnaires' Disease during the Bicentennial — the mysterious illness that baffled scientists and changed public health forever.

events.title: Just Us
events.description: Original works by artists at SCI Phoenix and justice-impacted artists from Mural Arts Philadelphia’s Rec Crew.

events.title: Marcel Duchamp
events.description: The first North American retrospective of Marcel Duchamp's work in over 50 years. Spanning painting, sculpture, film, photography, drawings, and printed matter across six decades of the artist's multifaceted career.

events.title: The Great Gatsby
events.description: THE GREAT GATSBY is a “Broadway extravaganza that explodes with life and energy” (Entertainment Weekly). Based on the classic American novel by F. Scott Fitzgerald, the Tony Award®-winning new musical is an unforgettable journey of love, wealth and tragedy that brings the Roaring Twenties to life on stage.

events.title: Yunchan Lim Plays Rachmaninoff
events.description: “Superlatives cluster around Yunchan Lim,” The Guardian writes of the dazzling star who returns to thrill us again. He will perform Rachmaninoff’s blazing Third Piano Concerto, the work that spurred his win as the youngest pianist ever to win the coveted Van Cliburn Competition Gold Medal.

events.title: Prohibition: Then and Now
events.description: How did alcohol prohibition come into law and what are the connections to present day drug policy? Join us as Kelsey Leon, harm reductionist, anthropologist, and clinical research coordinator, discusses the impact of prohibition on the drug economy and on people who use criminalized substances.

events.title: FAMILY FUNDRAISER
events.description: Calling all curious kiddos, playful parents, and thrill-seeking families! FunFest: A Night at the Museum is your golden ticket to an after-hours adventure where the museum turns into your playground.

events.title: The Bad Plus Farewell Tour
events.description: For the past two decades The Bad Plus have played with spirit and adventure, made their own rules and done so with a bold sense of creativity and intent.

events.title: BOOP!® The Musical
events.description: For almost a century, the Betty Boop® character has won hearts and inspired fans around the world with her trademark looks, voice, and style.

events.title: Handel’s Messiah
events.description: Handel’s transcendent choral masterwork is a highlight of the holiday season, gathering friends and family in what, for many, is an unmissable annual tradition. From poignant arias to blazing choruses—including the indomitable “Hallelujah” chorus—Messiah is a perennial holiday favorite for its thrilling drama and operatic breadth.

events.title: Children’s Holiday Spectacular
events.description: Bring the whole family and enjoy a concert designed for all ages, filled with familiar music and a few fun surprises along the way. And keep an ear out for sleigh bells—you never know who might stop by from the North Pole.

events.title: Bach’s Christmas Oratorio
events.description: Immerse yourself in Bach’s monumental Christmas Oratorio, a collection of six spectacular cantatas written for the six feasts between Christmas and the Epiphany, heard complete for the first time by The Philadelphia Orchestra. From triumphant fanfares to sweet lullabies to glorious choruses, Bach’s brilliance shines through every single movement.

events.title: Pink Martini All-Stars present A Season of Stars
events.description: Thomas Lauderdale's globe-trotting "little orchestra" Pink Martini is back with an all-new holiday show that brings triple the joy! Featuring three of the band's favorite singers and long-time collaborators, the Pink Martini All-Stars present: A Season of Stars tour conjures up a mix of old holiday favorites and sweet new treats, glittering…

events.title: Operation Mincemeat: A New Musical
events.description: How did a dead body, a fake love letter, and — of all people — Ian Fleming turn the tide of World War II? Olivier Award winner for Best New Musical and a 2025 Tony® winner, Operation Mincemeat: A New Musical is the best-reviewed show in West End history with…

events.title: Ben Folds with The Philadelphia Orchestra
events.description: 2026-27 Season Ben Folds with The Philadelphia Orchestra A Benefit Concert for the Musicians’ Retirement Fund Dec 16, 2026 Marian Anderson Hall

events.title: The Glorious Sound of Christmas®
events.description: The Philadelphia Orchestra lends its iconic sound to timeless holiday classics! The Glorious Sound of Christmas is an annual Philadelphia tradition beloved by listeners of all ages and the perfect way to begin all holiday celebrations.

events.title: STOMP
events.description: The international percussion sensation has garnered armfuls of awards and rave reviews and has appeared on numerous national television shows. The eight-member troupe uses everything but conventional percussion instruments – matchboxes, wooden poles, brooms, garbage cans, Zippo lighters, hubcaps – to fill the stage with magnificent rhythms.

events.title: Noguchi to Asawa: Designing Postwar America
events.description: Iconic sculpture and design by two generations of Japanese American artists.

events.title: Sky Hopinka: Red Metal Dust
events.description: An installation of 11 new works by the American artist.

events.title: The Book of Mormon
events.description: The New York Times calls it “the best musical of this century. ” The Washington Post says, “It is the kind of evening that restores your faith in musicals. ” And Entertainment Weekly says, “Grade A: the funniest musical of all time.

events.title: Waitress
events.description: Meet Jenna, a waitress and expert pie-maker who dreams of a way out of her small town and rocky marriage. Pouring her heart into her pies, she crafts desserts that mirror her topsy-turvy life such as “The Key (Lime) to Happiness Pie” and “Betrayed By My Eggs Pie.

events.title: Yohay Sponder: Genesis
events.description: Yohay Sponder is an Israeli bilingual standup comedian turned international sensation. With over 20 years of experience, Sponder brings his optimistic outlook on life to the stage.

events.title: PAW Patrol Live! "A Mighty Adventure"
events.description: Ensemble Arts Presents in association with VStar Entertainment Group PAW Patrol Live! "A Mighty Adventure" Feb 20 - Feb 21, 2027 Academy Of Music

events.title: Peter and the Wolf
events.description: Prokofiev’s Peter and the Wolf returns, introducing audiences to the instruments of the orchestra through a simple, engaging tale of a boy’s adventure in the woods.

events.title: Rochelle Feinstein: The Today Show
events.description: More than 30 mixed-media works examining abstraction, culture, and public life.

events.description: Explore the experiences of a diverse group of scholars whose education was supported by the Barnes.

events.title: Gary Gulman's 7th Hour
events.description: Following the success of his critically acclaimed one-man show, Grandiloquent, Gary Gulman returns with his all-new stand-up show 7th Hour. Over 30 years in comedy, Gary Gulman has established himself as an eminent performer and peerless writer.

events.title: MARVEL STUDIOS' BLACK PANTHER IN CONCERT
events.description: Marvel Studios' Black Panther in Concert features a screening of the groundbreaking film electrified by live performances from world-class Hollywood studio musicians, African rhythm masters and powerhouse vocalists, delivering the award-winning score and soundtrack in a truly unforgettable experience.

events.title: Riverdance 30 - The New Generation
events.description: Experience the original phenomenon. A thrilling celebration of music and dance, Riverdance returns in a spectacular new production with Grammy Award-winning music, breathtaking choreography, and explosive energy.

events.title: Oh, Mary!
events.description: Oh, Mary! is a dark comedy about a miserable, suffocated Mary Todd Lincoln in the weeks leading up to Abraham Lincoln’s assassination. Unrequited yearning, alcoholism, and suppressed desires abound in this 80-minute one-act play that finally examines the forgotten life and dreams of Mrs.

events.title: Chloé Arnold's Syncopated Ladies Live!
events.description: Syncopated Ladies Live! is a ground-breaking mixed-media concert for theatergoers of all ages featuring a diverse all-female cast celebrating sisterhood, the power of joy, and tap dance! Get to know the ladies as they share their inspiring journeys to reach for their dreams through the art of tap dance.

events.title: Green Eggs and Ham
events.description: Do you like Green Eggs and Ham? This orchestral adaptation of Dr. Seuss's beloved children's classic is a feast for the ears! The inimitable Michael Boudewyns as Sam-I-Am serves up a veritable banquet of surprises in Robert Kapilow's culinary cartoon-musical banquet.

events.title: Sh!t-faced Shakespeare® Macbeth
events.description: "By the pricking of my thumbs, something wicked [tipsy] this way comes. " An entirely serious production of William Shakespeare's Macbeth with an entirely sh!t-faced cast member. Shakespeare's tale of murder, ambition, bloodlust, and supernatural.

events.title: Inside the Music: Let 'Em Eat Cake
events.description: Explore the music of the Gershwins' dystopian farce Let 'Em Eat Cake, coming to the Academy of Music January 29-31, at this engaging talk with Opera Philadelphia's Scholar-in-Residence Dr. Lily Kass.

events.title: Let ’Em Eat Cake
events.description: An American president loses reelection, decides to overthrow the new government, and then redesigns the White House. This is the story of George and Ira Gershwin’s 1933 musical that aims its barbs at everything from totalitarianism to fashion shows.

events.title: This calendar features events presented by FringeArts!
events.description: Throughout the year, FringeArts curates and presents a series of performances and events by local, national, and international contemporary artists. We also host workshops, works-in-progress, and community events. Click here to learn more about FringeArts.

events.title: Topdog/Underdog
events.description: Brothers Lincoln and Booth, whose names foreshadow a lifetime of rivalry and resentment, share a single room, pass the time telling stories, testing each other, and circling the street con game of three-card monte as they grapple with their futures. Topdog/Underdog is co-produced with People’s Light.

events.title: Native Gardens
events.description: Tania and her husband Pablo think they’ve found the American dream when they move next door to Virginia and Frank, longtime residents with a picture-perfect garden. But a backyard gathering and a question about the fence line quickly ignite a hilarious feud, exposing their clashing ideas of taste, class, and culture.

events.title: John Proctor is the Villain
events.description: At a rural Georgia high school, a group of juniors are just trying to survive sex ed, hallway gossip, and the chaos of growing up. But when their English class begins reading The Crucible, the classroom becomes a battleground for the truth as the students start asking uncomfortable questions about Salem and the men history calls heroes

events.title: Kimberly Akimbo
events.description: Kimberly is about to turn 16, but a rare condition causes her to age rapidly, making her look decades older. As she navigates family dysfunction, her first crush, and possible felony charges, Kimberly remains determined to find happiness.

events.description: Thursday Showtimes 6:30PM & 9:00PM | Friday & Saturday Showtimes 7:00PM & 9:30PMSaxophonist Kim Waters captivates jazz lovers with his smooth contemporary sound. Gaining fame in the 1990s with albums like "Sax Appeal," his hit "What I Like" reached No. 3 on the charts in 2018. He honored Marvin Gaye with "I Want You: Love in the Spirit of Marvin" in 2008. After debuting with "Sweet and Saxy" in 1989, Waters showcased his artistry in the 2022 release "That Special Touch," featuring his daughter, Kayla Waters.

events.title: PHER | Sun Nov 8 | 6:00PM & 8:30PM
events.description: Oakland-born vocalist, songwriter, and three-time Grammy-winning collaborator bringing jazz-level musicianship into soul and alternative R&B. PHER is an Oakland-born vocalist, songwriter, and three-time Grammy-winning collaborator whose voice has appeared on award-winning work by Esperanza Spalding and Jon Batiste. His credits include Prince, Snarky Puppy, Chief Adjuah, Kanye West, Lupe Fiasco, Kris Bowers, Eric Harland, James Francies, and the SFJAZZ Collective. He co-wrote and recorded “We Are America” with Prince and Esperanza Spalding, and delivered the featured vocal performance on Snarky Puppy’s “Liquid Love.” Longtime listeners first knew him as Chris Turner. events.title: SPUR OF THE MOMENT | THURSDAY NOVEMBER 12 | presented by UNSCRIPTED JAZZ
events.description: In a volatile industry where passions wax and wane, the trends of today become the clichés of tomorrow, and bands split as quickly as they capture the world’s hearts; Spur Of The Moment has, over the past two decades, bucked the odds, transcended the usual ups and downs, and inspired thousands of fans across the world with a vibe that continues to define the word band.The list of artists that have worked with this immensely talented unit grows yearly. Their resume reads like a "who’s who" of the R&B and Jazz worlds. From the legendary George Duke to Al Jarreau, Patti Austin, Ledisi, Raheem Devaughn, and Lalah Hathaway.

events.description: FRIDAY & SATURDAY SHOWTIMES 7:00PM & 9:30PM SUNDAY SHOWTIMES 6:00PM & 8:30PMFounded by acclaimed bassist and composer Warren Oree, The Arpeggio Jazz Ensemble has established a lasting presence in the world of contemporary jazz through its signature sound known as “Undefeated Jazz.” For more than four decades, the ensemble has blended original compositions, jazz standards, world rhythms, and improvisational energy into performances that are both artistically sophisticated and deeply engaging. The ensemble’s sound moves seamlessly from intimate, reflective melodies to dynamic, rhythm-driven performances. This versatility allows Arpeggio to tailor performances for concert halls, festivals, educational programs, private events, and community celebrations

events.title: CHRIS "BIG DOG" DAVIS | THURSDAY NOVEMBER 19 | presented by UNSCRIPTED JAZZ
events.description: Christopher J. Davis, fondly known a "Big Dog", was born in Waterbury, Connecticut to musical parents James Sr. and Mary Davis. When Chris was just four years old he had the ability to hear music in a special way. He began his piano studies at age five gripping the origins of black music at the Refuge Church of Christ in his hometown. By age sixteen, Chris recorded his first forty-five gospel where he began fusing gospel, funk, classical and jazz which he has perfected into an eclectic style all his own today.Chris is a two-time Grammy nominated writer and producer and has 15 Billboard top #1 smooth jazz records since 2008. Chris ‘Big Dog’ Davis has received a Grammy nomination in 2014 for his work with singer/songwriter “Maysa” on her Blue Velvet Soul CD.

events.title: JEFF BRADSHAW | FRI, SAT & SUN NOV 20, 21 & 22 | SHOWTIMES VARY BY DAY
events.description: Step into the world of trombone-powered soul, jazz, hip-hop, and R&B. Inspired by his father, a gifted musician and vocalist, Jeff was immersed in horn-driven sound from a young age. While his early instruments of choice were the baritone horn and sousaphone, it was the often-overlooked trombone that ultimately spoke to him.In high school, Jeff’s curiosity led him to explore this underappreciated instrument.
